result.instructions: Tools for Zenserp, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "What are the top search results for 'best coffee roaster Prague'?"; "Find coffee shops near Leeds city centre with their ratings and phone numbers."; "What is the latest news about electric delivery vans?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Zenserp data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run zenserp_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run zenserp_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run zenserp_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. zenserp_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: zenserp_get_status
tools.title: Get remaining requests
tools.description: The number of search requests left on this Zenserp key's plan (remaining_requests). Free: it spends no quota. GET /v2/status.

tools.name: zenserp_search
tools.title: Search the web (SERP)
tools.description: Live search-engine result page as JSON: organic results, ads (paid_results), featured snippets, related questions and searches, knowledge graph. Google by default; set search_engine for Bing, Yandex or DuckDuckGo. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. ai_overview=true also returns Google's AI Overview and costs 3 requests when one is returned (Small plan or higher). GET /v2/search.

q.description: The query; search operators such as site: and intitle: work.

search_engine.description: Search engine host, e.g. google.com (default), google.de, bing.com, yandex.com, duckduckgo.com. zenserp_list_search_engines lists them.

hl.description: Interface language (hl), e.g. en, de, pt-BR. zenserp_list_languages lists the supported codes.

gl.description: Country (gl), two letters, e.g. us, de, gb. zenserp_list_countries lists the supported codes. Default: United States.

lr.description: Limit results to these languages (lr), prefixed with lang_ and joined by |, e.g. lang_fr.

location.description: Geolocation of the search, in Google's canonical form, e.g. 'Manhattan,New York,United States' (see zenserp_search_locations). Set it when the result depends on place, especially ads.

start.description: Result offset: 0 (default) first page, 10 second page, 20 third page ... Google serves about 300 results per query.

tbs.description: Google 'tbs' filter string for what the query field cannot express, e.g. qdr:w (past week).

ai_overview.description: true = also extract Google's AI Overview (3 requests when returned, otherwise 1; slower; Google only; Small plan or higher).

cache.description: true = serve a stored copy when one exists (kept 24 h, NOT charged) and store the reply when not. Default false: every call is fetched live and charged.

fields.description: Only return these top-level keys of the reply (for example organic, paid_results, related_searches). Saves context; the call is charged the same.

tools.name: zenserp_flights
tools.title: Search Google Flights
tools.description: Google Flights options. Best: origin and destination as 3-letter airport codes plus departure_date (dates and curr are honoured only then). A free-text q or a tfs string from a Google Flights URL also works. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/flights.

origin.description: Departure airport code, e.g. JFK. Name one airport, not a city.

departure_date.description: Departure date, yyyy-mm-dd. Needs origin and destination.

return_date.description: Return date, yyyy-mm-dd. Omit for one-way.

curr.description: 3-letter currency code for the prices, e.g. USD.

q.description: Free-text flight query, used when no airport codes are given (no dates, no curr).

tfs.description: Google Flights search string copied from a Google Flights URL (full filters).

cache.description: true = serve a stored copy when one exists (kept 24 h, NOT charged) and store the reply when not. Default false: every call is fetched live and charged.

fields.description: Only return these top-level keys of the reply (for example organic, paid_results, related_searches). Saves context; the call is charged the same.

tools.name: zenserp_trends
tools.title: Get Google Trends
tools.description: Trending searches from Google Trends for a country, optionally narrowed to given keywords or a category. Trending data covers at most the past 7 days. SPENDS 1 request of the monthly quota per successful call (failed calls are not charged); do not repeat a call needlessly. GET /v1/trends.

keyword.description: Only trends matching these terms (and their related queries). A term that is not trending returns no rows.

cat.description: Google Trends category id, e.g. 16 News, 7 Finance, 18 Shopping, 20 Sports, 5 Computers & Electronics, 45 Health.

timeframe.description: Window; longer ones all return the same 7-day window for trending searches.

cache.description: true = serve a stored copy when one exists (kept 24 h, NOT charged) and store the reply when not. Default false: every call is fetched live and charged.

fields.description: Only return these top-level keys of the reply (for example organic, paid_results, related_searches). Saves context; the call is charged the same.

tools.name: zenserp_answer_engine
tools.title: Ask an AI answer engine
tools.description: Send a prompt to an AI answer engine (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Copilot) and get its answer_text with citations; with brand it also reports whether and where that brand was cited. SPENDS quota at Zenserp's premium per-answer rate (see Zenserp pricing), is slow (seconds to a minute), and must not be repeated needlessly. Plan gate: Medium unlocks ChatGPT, Large adds Perplexity, Premium adds Gemini, Enterprise adds Copilot. GET /v1/answer-engine.

prompt.description: The question or prompt. prompt and additional_prompt together may hold at most 4,096 characters.

additional_prompt.description: An optional follow-up prompt sent with the main one (counts toward the 4,096-character limit shared with prompt).

country.description: Two-letter country code to localise the answer, e.g. us.

brand.description: A brand name to track: the reply then has a brand_visibility object.

fields.description: Only return these top-level keys of the reply (for example organic, paid_results, related_searches). Saves context; the call is charged the same.

tools.name: zenserp_search_locations
tools.title: Search geo locations
tools.description: The supported geo locations (values for location), as Google's canonical names. The list is long: pass query to keep only entries that contain it, and limit to cap the count. GET /v2/locations.

query.description: Keep only entries whose text contains this (case-insensitive), e.g. 'vienna'.
